the role of the ER stress sensor, IRE-1, in dendrite morphogenetic processes in the nematodes C. elegans and D. melanogaster, and in rat hippocampal neuron culture.
the regulation of dendritic arborization in the nervous system, and in particular with the role of Ire1 in dendrite morphogenensis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ire1/XBP-1 axis is essential for dendrite morphogenesis in C. elegans PVD neurons.

the IRE-1/XBP-1 pathway is not required for normal PVD dendrite morphology, but that the IRE1 nuclease is required for normal Pvd dendrite morphology, and that the Insulin/IGFR pathway is required for normal IRE-1 nuclease activity.

the Ire1/Xbp1 pathway is required for proper dendrite morphogenesis and that this function of Ire1 is independent of the Xbp1 transcriptional target, but rather depends on the ability of Ire1 to sense ER stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ire1 is required for dendritic arborization in neurons, but the mechanism is independent of the best characterized Ire1 target Xbp1.
IRE- 1 is a conserved ER stress sensor that controls dendrite branching by regulating the secretion and localization of DMA-1.
IRE- 1 regulates dendrite arbor formation in a conserved fashion, which is independent from its role in the unfolded protein response (UPR).
The main takeaway from our work is that
IRE- 1 is a key ER stress sensor in the nervous system, which regulates neuronal dendritic morphogenesis.
the ER stress sensor Ire1/IRE-1 plays a role in dendrite patterening in both nematode and rat neurons.
Ire1 is necessary for proper neuronal branching and dendrite morphogenesis in C. elegans and rat hippocampal cells.
